blocks.title: Strategic Trade Advisory for Regional & Continental Markets
blocks.body: With 23+ years of customs and logistics expertise in East African trade, Kenya Tradex provides strategic consulting to help businesses navigate the complex landscape of regional and continental trade agreements. Whether you're exporting to Uganda, Rwanda, or looking to access the broader African market under AfCFTA, we provide actionable guidance.
items: East African Community (EAC): Deep integration among 7 member states with common external tariff, free movement of goods, and zero duty on qualifying EAC-origin goods. Savings: Up to 35% on import duties.

African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA): World's largest free trade area by population (1.4 billion people, $3.4 trillion GDP). Phased tariff reductions across 54 countries. Strategic opportunity for Kenyan exporters.
COMESA (Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa): 21 member states with existing preferential trade arrangements. Complementary to EAC and AfCFTA.

blocks.title: EAC vs AfCFTA: Which Trade Agreement Works for You?
blocks.body: *AfCFTA implementation is phased. Kenya Tradex provides readiness assessments for businesses looking to leverage AfCFTA opportunities.

blocks.title: Strategic Markets We Cover
blocks.body: Plus AfCFTA markets: Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, and 48 other African nations. We help you identify priority markets based on your product and strategy.

blocks.title: Our Cross-Border Consulting Services
items: Trade Agreement Analysis – Which agreement (EAC, AfCFTA, COMESA) offers the best duty savings for your product?
Rules of Origin Advisory – Determine eligibility and complete Certificates of Origin for preferential rates.
Tariff Classification (HS Code) – Correct classification to maximize savings and ensure compliance.
Market Entry Strategy – Regulatory requirements, logistics planning, and partner identification.
Export Documentation – Complete paperwork for customs clearance (Certificate of Origin, Form C, IDF, Bill of Lading).
AfCFTA Readiness Assessment – Evaluate your business for continental trade opportunities.
Transit Bond Management – For cargo moving through Kenya to landlocked EAC countries.
Regulatory Compliance – Stay ahead of changing EAC and AfCFTA requirements.

blocks.title: How our cross-border consulting works
items: Step 1: Initial consultation to understand your product, target markets, and trade goals.
Step 2: Trade agreement analysis and rules of origin assessment for your product.
Step 3: Duty and tax optimization strategy using preferential rates (EAC, AfCFTA, COMESA).
Step 4: Documentation preparation (Certificate of Origin, Form C, IDF, Bill of Lading).
Step 5: Ongoing compliance monitoring and market expansion support.

blocks.title: Cross-border trade questions
items:
What is AfCFTA and how can my business benefit? 
The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) creates a single continental market for goods and services, covering 1.4 billion people with a combined GDP of $3.4 trillion. Kenyan businesses can access preferential duty rates when exporting to 54 African countries. Kenya Tradex provides AfCFTA readiness assessments and rules of origin guidance.

How can I benefit from EAC rules of origin? 
EAC rules of origin allow qualifying goods to be imported at zero or reduced duty rates within the East African Community. Kenya Tradex helps you determine eligibility, complete the Certificate of Origin, and maximize your duty savings.

What documents are required for cross-border trade from Kenya? 
Key documents include a Certificate of Origin (for EAC or AfCFTA preferential rates), Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Bill of Lading, Transit Bond, and Customs Declaration. Kenya Tradex handles all documentation for seamless cross-border movement.

What is the difference between EAC and AfCFTA? 
EAC (East African Community) is a regional bloc of 7 countries with deeper integration including a common external tariff. AfCFTA is a continent-wide agreement covering 54 countries, phasing in over time. Both offer preferential duty rates but with different rules of origin. Kenya Tradex helps navigate both frameworks.

What is a transit bond and why do I need it? 
A transit bond is a customs guarantee that allows cargo to move from Mombasa port to landlocked EAC countries without paying import duties until final destination. Kenya Tradex manages transit bonds for Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, DRC, and South Sudan.
